findings.title: BlackLotus UEFI bootkit: Myth confirmed
findings.summary_md: ESET researchers published the first in-the-wild analysis of BlackLotus, confirming it uses the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to bypass UEFI Secure Boot on fully patched Windows 11 systems. The report notes BlackLotus had been advertised on underground forums since at least October 6, 2022, for $5,000. This is the earliest credible technical confirmation of the bootkit.

findings.title: Guidance for investigating attacks using CVE-2022-21894: The BlackLotus campaign
findings.summary_md: Microsoft's security blog detailed investigation steps for BlackLotus, describing how the bootkit exploits CVE-2022-21894 to deploy malicious files to the EFI System Partition (ESP) and achieve pre-OS persistence. The guidance confirms active exploitation concerns and provides detection recommendations for defenders.
